en: Śākyamuni Buddha praises the Assistant Dalai of Chankhufu Temple,
a Tangut scholar-instructor serving in the Inner Court Qingzi Jingshuan (Palace Institute for Tibetan Studies).
At the three times, he releases all enmity; at the attainment of enlightenment, he subdues both nāgas and gandharvas.
All pay homage to the Honored One who wears precious ornaments;
beneath his wondrous, majestic lotus feet, radiant golden light shines forth from his body of awesome power. His voice is the exquisite melody of the gandharvas, beyond compare.
The World-Honored Śākyamuni, whose mind is as pure and clear as a billion suns, guides all sentient beings.
Like the various constellations arrayed across the clear sky, he shines everywhere throughout the ocean of existence with total lucidity.
Within the sea of sincere intent, his myriad virtuous forms are distinct and peerless, manifesting with ultimate clarity.
The fingers support one another, held at the heart; like the moon reflecting upon a small pool of water, the single mind manifests before the Honored One’s body.
With a slight praise, I pray for the World-Honored One’s compassion, surrounded by heroic Bodhisattvas and a gathering of Arhats arrayed before him.
Like stars in the sky all bowing toward the moon, Like the preeminent leader among a herd of oxen,
with light appearing as a thousand-spoked wheel encircling his body; His radiance fills the entire realm of space,
Performing various miraculous transformations without hindrance, He arrives like a king of swans, flying down to descend.
At that time, due to the virtuous deeds cultivated in the past, hundreds of thousands of devas and humans were ready for maturation;
upon beholding the Honored One’s countenance, they were immediately liberated.
Having cast off all fetters and a hundredfold transgressions, he sat with heroic valor beneath the Bodhi tree, subduing the Lord of Māra with the weapons of compassion and wisdom.
His majestic power has completely subdued all, just as a fierce wind sweeps away dark clouds;
without armor or weapons, he alone has achieved total victory over billions of māras without exception.
Apart from the Honored One, who else could do this?
The World-Honored One is a compassionate fire that intensely burns away the minds of those in the desire realm;
he is an ocean of loving-kindness toward sentient beings, impartial toward both kin and strangers.
For the sake of benefiting all living beings, he never tires for even a moment.
Sentient beings before the Honored One recite his virtues without weariness;
his depth is unfathomable like the ocean, and his speech is sublime and wondrous like the sound of a celestial drum.
His supreme body appears like the summit of Mount Sumeru; seeing, hearing, remembering, or thinking of him is never in vain.
All sentient beings throughout all worlds, Simultaneously inquire about their doubts;
To each and every one of them, as many as there are, He simultaneously manifests his body and speech—
The secret principles of the noble body, speech, and mind— To the bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and arhats.
Even if one were to observe it, it is not an object of ordinary cognition; how much less so for Śakra, Brahmā, or those of the world?
Like the king of golden-winged garuḍas traversing the void, when his strength is exhausted, he merely stops and turns back;
yet the void itself knows no end. So too it is with the description of the Buddha’s virtues.
Just as a great garuḍa spreads its wings and flies, while a tiny sparrow on the path strives in vain to follow; so too,
though one may wish to enter the sphere traversed by the Sovereign of Ten Powers upon that supreme path,
the eye of wisdom that perceives the ultimate truth is blind, and the mind of renunciation for awakening is exhausted.
The powerful enemy of afflictions constantly harasses me, And repeatedly casts me into the deep pit of self-grasping.

Such a state of defilement and humiliation is truly lamentable; Even if the Compassionate Honored One were to abandon me once more, To whom could I turn for refuge, and who but You would hold me with great compassion and pity for those who are lowly?
In this world of the five turbidities, amidst its chaotic and impure conditions, when others have abandoned it, you, O Benevolent One, maintain it in its entirety;
all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas praise you, comparing you directly to the white lotus—what can be said now?
The deeds of the World-Honored One are for the sake of subduing and transforming beings; there is not even the slightest thing that he does not observe.
All is due to evil conditions and the sins I have committed myself; therefore, toward you, O Honored One, I have no fault.

From this day forth, I vow to cultivate bodhicitta, and until I attain the Way and subdue the Lord of Māras, may the World-Honored One always protect me throughout every birth, and may I receive the nectar of your words without ever growing weary.

The above is the hymn of praise for Śākyamuni, which serves as the cause for swift gathering [of merit]. It was composed by the disciple Tripiṭakadhara Jñānakumāra at the shrine of the deity Lha btsun mgon po in the cave of Brag lha sding ba in the Snow Mountains of Tibet, through the request of the learned and virtuous master named Ye shes mgon po.
How is the Tathāgata’s essence so subtle? What are his retinue, his lifespan, his realm, and what is his name? We pray that we all may likewise become so;
we praise the power of the World-Honored One’s subtle goodness wherever we may be.
May disease, demons, poverty, and strife be entirely eliminated; May all increase in virtue and auspiciousness be granted.
May all Buddhas arise in the world, And may the holy teachings shine forth like the light of the sun.
May those who uphold the teachings be in harmony like brothers; I pray that the sublime Dharma bestow eternal auspiciousness.
The twelve lines above are a prayer for those who recite; they may be chanted following the preceding hymn of praise.
The praise to Śākyamuni Buddha is concluded.
